title: Which ramp is steeper?
hook: Two ramps start from the same foot. Which one is steeper?

knows: reading points on a simple grid or graph
doesNotKnow: slope as rise per run, a ratio

misconception: A line that climbs higher is steeper.
objective: The learner can compare steepness by the climb over the same distance across (rise / run), and explain why a ramp rising 2 over 4 is steeper than one rising 3 over 12.

claims.text: Steepness (slope) is the rise divided by the run: how far a line climbs per step across.
claims.source: Definition of the slope of a line, m = rise / run = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1).

claims.text: Ramp A rises 3 over 12, a slope of 0.25; ramp B rises 2 over 4, a slope of 0.5, twice as steep.
Over the same 4 across, A climbs 1 and B climbs 2; kept going for 12 across, B would climb 6.
claims.source: 0.25 x 4 = 1, 0.5 x 4 = 2, 0.5 x 12 = 6; the stage computes the climbs from the same slopes; recomputed with node. | v2 (2026-10-14): title no longer states the answer; reveal gated on both the 4-across and 12-across lines; previous verification void, needs re-check.

claims.text: Both ramps start at the same foot (the locked stage marks it: both ramps start here).
claims.source: Stage design in Demo.tsx: both ramps are drawn from (0, 0); while locked only the grid, the ground and that point are drawn. Added v3 2026-10-14 by demo-builder. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): VERIFIED. Demo: while locked only the grid, ground and a dot at (0, 0) labelled 'both ramps start here' are drawn; unlocked, both ramp lines start at px(0), py(0).

recall.question: Path P climbs 10 m over 100 m across. Path Q climbs 6 m over 30 m across. Which is steeper?
recall.why: Steepness is rise per run: P is 10 / 100 = 0.1, Q is 6 / 30 = 0.2. Q climbs twice as much per metre across, even though P ends higher.
